It takes all of your will and concentration to not let him just like run off and explore all the random things he sees in the forest.

But by keeping him on track, you manage to travel the 30 miles by, in about 12 hours. So, or even 10 hours, right? So you m- you get... It's like every, you know, he'll- he sees the berries, he wants to eat the berries. He wants to go play in the river. He wants to like chase the birds. He's never seen a forest before. He's like super excited by it. But you like keep encouraging him that, "Oh, there's more of that this way. You can go this way and you'll get it."
Until you come. This clearing is obvious when you f- when you find it. Um— Mm... you, you do, I will say just for simplicity, you, you send, you beast sense a bird and get it to fly up-
DM: ... so you can find where the clearing is. Um, you seem to have actually beat Theba.

before: DM: ... you're like totally. Make a animal handling check with advantage.
Seeker: There is a little bit of vulnerability of Wellby being by himself carrying all of this when there's a dragon around.
Delwath: There is. But he's moving fast.
DM: And he's-
Wellby: Uh, 24.
after: Seeker: Yeah.
DM: She said she'd meet you in two days time, which would be tomorrow morning.
Kenzo: Yeah.
DM: That makes sense. It's okay.
Seeker: Stone bunker.

interactions.title: The torn warning at dawn
lines: Delwath: That's a pretty big mobilization. I'm gonna scry with my two dawn scrys. The first one is I'm gonna scry the tree. Has anybody been there? Is it disturbed at all? Has anybody taken the letter? Has, like, anything changed?
DM: Um, the, the letter is, um, is... So the graves have been, more offerings have been added.
DM: And the letter is torn up on the ground.
Delwath: Interesting. Are the offerings that we left disturbed?
DM: The monument is still there.
Delwath: So there's new offerings, our offerings are gone.
DM: And the letter has been torn up and it's scattered. It's like, almost like somebody grounded into the ground with their heel.
Delwath: Is there any sign that the graves have been disturbed?
Delwath: Is there any sign that a lot of people have been here?
DM: Yeah, you can't really tell. I mean, definitely, clearly somebody's been here.
DM: But it's really hard to gauge the numbers.

before: DM: You can see 10 tents within range of your darkvision. It's quite dark underneath the forest.
Delwath: Yeah, okay.
DM: There's-
Delwath: So it's not a small... I mean, does it look like the edge of the encampment? Does it look like it keeps going?
DM: It's hard to tell. But it's at least 10, potentially somewhat more than that. There's one other person sleeping in this tent with this guy, so probably at least 20.
after: Delwath: Okay, last scry. What should I scry?
DM: Hmm, maybe Theba.
Delwath: She's gonna be showing up here any minute in theory.
Kenzo: If she's still alive.
Delwath: But I can always short rest again. I mean, I'll have the last scry and I'll actually have full sl- spell slots. Like, that's giving myself a short rest as well in the course of the night.

interactions.title: Theba meets the party and offers a refuge
lines: DM: Um, when Theba comes into the, uh, clearing, um, she's carrying her, her spear and shield. Um, she's moving quickly, but like looking around. Um, uh, she's found a chain shirt somewhere, not as nice as the breastplate, but some armor.

Um, and, uh, she's run- she's running as she enters the clearing, and she, when she sees your camp, she stops for a minute and walks, walks over to you and says, "You beat me. Impressive. What is... Are you ready to go? Should we find the Te'kula?"
Kenzo: And, and it's a "yes, and." It is a "yes, and."
Seeker: Um, did you know that, uh, Mezzar was a dragon?
Seeker: We confronted him, and he very nearly destroyed us all.
Kenzo: And killed six Deno'qai in the process.
Wellby: It was not a great day.
DM: One of our own was ki- [laughs]
Kenzo: That's what's so funny about this.
DM: I did not expect, did not expect that.
Kenzo: We did not either, and we barely escaped with our lives.
DM: I knew he was trouble somehow.
Kenzo: The Conclave, do you believe they still exist?
DM: I believe dragons still exist.
Seeker: But there could be more out there.
DM: Are you hurt? Does anybody need healing?
Seeker: Oh, we long rested, so yeah.
Wellby: But it is nice to travel with someone with healing.
Seeker: Yeah. That's true. That's a good call.
Seeker: But we're glad that your rendezvous point worked and we're able to meet up and travel together. We'll be stronger. Because, uh, Mezzar is undoubtedly hunting us now.
Delwath: Yeah, he... I mean, I'll share what I saw with scrying with you guys when we, everybody wakes up. There's a party of at least 20 or maybe more Deno'qai, uh, in the woods already camped.
Kenzo: Did you try to scry on Mezzar himself?
Delwath: I don't know. He has a high save.
Seeker: Yeah, it's just gonna be...
Delwath: But I mean, it's not a bad idea. I have plenty more opportunities to try.
Kenzo: Yeah, let's definitely do that-
Kenzo: ... 'cause if you get lucky, we can maybe sort of-
Delwath: I mean, I can do it right now.
Kenzo: ... like honestly, the Deno'qai soldiers, like kinda not who cares, but we should be able to take 'em, right?
Kenzo: If they catch... I mean, it's like, it's like where's the green dragon that can kill us all? That, that's kind of a...
Seeker: We, we only had a little time, but we tried to leave information by the God Tree telling the story of, uh, Mezzar being a dragon, but-
DM: They will not believe that.
Seeker: ... the Deno'qai are probably still under his thrall. Do you think there's anyone back at the village you could persuade to join us?
DM: I think the Te'kula know something. They have been hidden in secret paths in some dream realm for a generation.
DM: [coughs] I have traveled that way once before. I can take you again, and I wonder if they fled there to hide from this creature.
Kenzo: I under—when and when did, when did Meskar, Mezzar appear?
DM: About 10 or 15 years ago, about 10 years ago.
Delwath: But 30 years ago is when Rai's protection would have faded.
Delwath: Assuming Rai lost his ability to protect them, um, when he, when he failed to heal the world, at least.
Seeker: I've glimpsed the dream world. I'm interested to learn more how we can travel there.
Wellby: Let's go with all speed.
Seeker: But is this a place we go on foot, or do you have a different way?

DM: We go on foot. It's about a three-day journey from here. Although I know the path, only the forest can decide who is allowed to enter the realm of the Te'kula. So we will have to trust to the forest that it will let you pass.
Seeker: One of us, Kenzo, has communed with the forest.
DM: I heard. That's why I spoke to you in the first place.
Seeker: Perhaps that will help our cause.
DM: I believe we should travel quickly.
Seeker: Is there a way we can remain hidden from the dragon's eye?
DM: I have no such way to do, to do that.
Seeker: And the Deno'qai hunting us over land?
Delwath: I could not tell how far they were.
DM: They were camped at night, though. They hunted-
Seeker: We're likely, we're likely well ahead.
DM: We're likely well ahead, yes. I think if we move quickly under the cover of the forest, we can stay ahead of them.

before: Delwath: Get ready to go.

DM: Okay, so around a couple hour, an hour, say two hours past dawn, like maybe 8:00 in the morning, um, everybody's rested. You can all take long rests. You wake up. Um, you're sitting around, I assume no fire.
Seeker: No.
DM: But Delwath maybe made something cold for breakfast.
Delwath: Yes.
after: DM: "Okay, let us go."
Um, so over the next three days, you run, you basically are running through the forest. Um... Um, Tim?
Delwath: Yeah? I don't think it's, like, super entertaining to, like, play out every single possible scry. Right. But Delwath is going to try to, is definitely gonna spend time scrying.
DM: So I mean, you are moving- To try and just- ... quickly, so you, you're not gonna have ti- you can basically get a handful of, you know, a few scrys a day because-
Delwath: Well, scrying plus only having to sleep four hours for a long rest.

interactions.title: Theba leads the final path
lines: DM: The, you, so after this, this time, you, you come, you come to a place, like the forest is getting incredibly close and tight now, like unnaturally so. Like the trees, these giant trees are growing, you know, a few feet apart from each other. And you're now going quite, even at a quick pa- like Baxter is, you can't even ride Baxter anymore. He's, like, picking his way through with you. Everybody's moving slowly. Like, the branches are almost feel like they're reaching out to you. And it's, it's dark. Everything is in dim light, almost no... It's, this is a much thicker forest.

And she says, um, and she's been casting, she's been blessing you every morning, so you, you've been getting these extra hit points every morning. And she says, she looks at you and she says, um, "We are passing through the final path now. I will lead the way. The trail twists and turns here and the forest will make its decision. But no matter what you see or hear, whatever it is, do not leave the path for any reason."
DM: She begins to walk and you follow her.

DM: And the, the path like twists, the only way forward twists and turns in unexpected ways. Um, sometimes passing through like the hollow of a massive trunk with the trees stretching up above you. Sometimes going over or even under massive roots. And as you're twisting and turning you see, um, every now and then you'll catch a glimpse of a, like a clearing.

And after a few that are empty you see, um, you see one and in the clearing you see Kaeso running, and he stops in the middle of the clearing looking frantically around, and a giant lightning elemental is chasing him. And then a bolt of lightning shoots out from this creature looking very similar to the one that you fought in Fausto's tower. Oh, fuck. And it strikes him and the bolt of lightning hits him in the back and he stumbles and begins to fall.
Wellby: Stay on the path. Stay on the path.
Kenzo: Um, am I tempted to do anything?
Kenzo: I mean, if I thi- I got the instructions to stay on the path, I'm gonna stay on the path. But-
DM: Okay. Keep walking. The image fades.
Wellby: Just gonna let him die, huh? [laughs]
Kenzo: All right. Kenzo saves Kaeso.
DM: You come, you see another clearing and you see Frankar standing looking at the sky, flames shooting out of his mouth and hands.
DM: Slowly burning to a crisp.
Seeker: Seeker stops walking to watch.
DM: He seems to be burning for an awfully long time, slowly fading. Slowly, five minutes go by, and he-
Wellby: Can we all see these?
DM: Yeah, you can all see these.
Seeker: That's Frankar. That's my brother.

DM: And the scene shifts in this clearing as you're watching it, and you can see it looks like you're lo- looking now into another world, a meadow of golden flowers that turn into butterflies and drift away, and then another flower blooms.

And a unicorn walks through and begins to wander through the meadow, grazing on these flowers, and each time it bends down to eat one, another bud pops and another butterfly flies off. So there are golden unicorns, golden butterflies flying around its head. And it looks directly at you and sort of beckons with its horn.
Seeker: I'm like looking around like, "Me? Uh, wow." Are, are, um, unicorns a thing?
DM: Yeah. I mean, they're fey creatures. They're-
DM: ... there, there's six conflicting descriptions of unicorns in Ultarn's book.
Seeker: Naturally. Does this match any of the six?
DM: Yeah. This is, this is description number three, a large white horse with flowing silver mane and a golden horn, um, with green eyes and, um, a piercing gaze, still beckoning you.
Seeker: I, I take a deep breath and say, "Not today, unicorn," and turn back to the path.

DM: Continue to walk till you see another clearing open up, a great tree standing in the center of the clearing, a glowing fragment of jade embedded in its trunk about 10 feet above the ground. The branches whisper, "Come. I will show you the secrets of the forest."
Seeker: Oh, we made it. This must be the destination. Is this, uh, is this directed to any one of us?
DM: All of you. Theba turns back and says, "Stay on the path."
Seeker: Fine, stay on the path. Okay. I look, um, as we're passing, just try to look closely at the jade to see what shape it is and how large it is and...
DM: It's too far away to really see clearly, and it seems to be glowing, so you only see this glow.
Seeker: Hmm. But it's definitely jade, a certain piece of jade embedded in that tree?

DM: It's, yeah. And you continue and you see a company of elves fighting hobgoblins at the edge of the woods, oblivious to archers sneaking through the meadow behind them. And as you watch, the archers stand and loose a volley of arrows that explode on impact, one elf dying and the rest turning, caught between fire and swords, outnumbered, slowly being hacked to pieces in this ambush.
Kenzo: Any sense of when this is?

DM: Theba. And you keep watching, and suddenly you come to a different forest. Like you step underneath a root and pass through a, the largest tree you've seen that's not one of these God trees. It's, it's like 20 feet in diameter maybe, and it almost looks like there's a door through its trunk. And you pass through this narrow tunnel, so maybe five feet tall, so only Wellby and Seeker can go standing. Baxter's like squirming his way through. Theba has to duck. You two have to duck.

And when you, when you step through this tree, you see ahead of you a clearing and a village. It looks very much like the Bek'eni village. It's set up in the same way. There's a long hall, um, little, uh, houses in the woods, a, um, a, a meadow, a clearing with a well, and a tree, uh, growing in the center of the, of the meadow.
Um, similar, similar style, right? So, coppice has many trunks. There's a small wooden altar in front of it. There are very few o- there are no offerings hanging from this tree.

DM: And, um, as you, as you step through and sort of approach, um, this, this forest, there is, um, there is a man sort of standing, waiting for you. His late 20s maybe, young, long blonde hair in dreadlocks, scubble- stubble on his face, strong and well-built, um, not armed or armored, but clearly could hold a spear. [coughs]
And he, he looks up as you approach, taking in Theba. Theba like, like bows, um, to him as, as she enters and, and says, uh, um, "Just please, may we enter?" And he looks over all of you.

before: Delwath: Okay.
DM: They're unchanged. And after a f- three days passing through this forest, the forest getting, um, Theba l- leading you into sort of a deeper, stiller part of the woods.

Delwath: All right, one other thing. Each dawn and evening too, I'm gonna find something to hunt for Aaviskar, and also continue my sort of reaching out to other gods to, to just try and open myself to hearing them.
DM: Okay.
Delwath: 'Cause I'm gonna multi-class into something that's religious, so might as well start playing around.
after: Kenzo: Before we continue, you guys want to take a break for lunch and/or...
DM: Yeah. That's a good idea.
Kenzo: It's a good, it's a good kind of a-
DM: Yeah.
Kenzo: ... you know, chapter moment before we start in with the next...

interactions.title: Belegor’s account of the elves, the dragon and the refuge
lines: DM: She has said she's, after learning that Mezzar was a dragon, she has to pray and think. And dinner is a somewhat boisterous affair without much chance for conversation.

But as the evening winds down, um, uh, Belegor the elf, Alayah, um, and a few others, um, come sit around the fire on the village green. Belegor particularly keen to hear Delwath's story, and Alayah kind of, uh, having spent so much of her childhood and her young life ensconced in these dreams, and now finally having met somebody else who has also experienced these, especially in the past... You get the sense that the past five years since Jordo died have not been easy for her.
So she is sort of following Kenzo around a little bit trying, you know, constantly asking him about, "Do you remember this? Do you remember that?"
DM: Finally having somebody to talk about what these things actually mean-

DM: ... has clearly had an impact on her. But everyb- as everybody settles down, um, Belegor, who is a, a tall elf, um, over six feet, 6'2", 6'3", like all of them ageless, um, with copper hair, short, relatively short cropped, um, wavy, uh, pale skin, green eyes, wearing sort of brown, brown, clothes in browns and reds, very autumnal colored, um, with a high collar and sleeves bound a- around his wrists by, like, gold threads.
Um, he, he turns to Delwath and he says, "I, I think perhaps we knew each other once in passing. You are of the 36th Kah, yes?"
DM: Generation. The 36th gener- 36th generation of elves ever to walk on the earth.
Seeker: Would Seeker already know about this kind of terminology or no?
Delwath: You probably haven't had that word before.
Seeker: So that was in character, I guess. [laughs]
DM: Yeah, and that's what Belegor says, is the 36th generation of elves to walk on this earth.
DM: I, I would ask the same of you. How did you come to be here?
Delwath: That's quite a story, which I'm happy to tell, but first tell me what has happened in the last 200 years.
Seeker: That's a ridiculous thing to say.
Kenzo: Pulls out a cold one.
DM: You, you know, you know not the tragedies of our people?
Delwath: No, not since the Great War.
DM: Like, you must know of the wars that followed.
DM: The dragon fire, the hobgoblins, the, the fight against the creeping darkness of the monsters of the Shadowfell spawned when Cha'mutte died.
Delwath: Only what I've heard. Been in Dunmar. We don't talk of what happened up north much there.
((table interruptions, repeated questions and unrelated planning))
Delwath: Volandeer. W- What has hap- I mean, that's where he's from too, obviously.
Delwath: Um, what has happened to Volandeer?
DM: Burned by dragon fire. Like many of the other great cities, Terrasa, Elintor, all destroyed.
Delwath: There are any left? I've seen-
Delwath: No elves save you since, uh, since returning to this place.

DM: Perhaps somewhere. Many of us came back from the wars scarred, hurt. [coughs] We mourn the destroyed cities. This is return from war to society changed, many lives lost, and many cities simply vanished. To where, we knew not.
Delwath: We've not been able to find them?
DM: Some think they fled to other planes, whole cities transported.
DM: We have searched the Feywild.
DM: Others think... Some of my generation, some of our generation, uh, think that many elves went to fight evil and protect this world across the multiverse and brought fortresses with them.

But personally, I believe that the unraveling that was started by Cha'mutte and never finished because he died still claimed those closest to his home, the furthest north cities. Holds where, I know not.
Seeker: Did you say defending the multiverse? Wha- what do you mean by that word?
DM: There are many planes not this, the Feywild, the Shadowfell, places like Arborea, the realms of the gods, the planes of fire and earth, air and water.
Seeker: I'm fascinated by and a student of these phenomena, but still an amateur, and you use that word to encompass them all?
Seeker: What does it mean to defend them?
DM: Well, the battles that were fought here are not necessarily the only battles of the Great War.
DM: I know not. But I believe if whole cities vanished, they vanished against their will, and the bulk of the elves may still be lost somewhere in some other plane.
Kenzo: How, how would a whole city vanish?

DM: The process of... The structure of this world is made of strands of many other planes captured and tamed, or so the elves teach. Cha'mutte sought to pull those apart to bring the other planes fully within this one.
DM: To collapse the boundaries that had kept reality stable for several lifetimes.
Seeker: When an elf says lifetime, they mean...
DM: Millennia, at least. If that process started and then was abruptly aborted, perhaps some parts of this world snapped to other planes.

And I still hope perhaps that a city of the elves, maybe Oromondi, one of our furthest north settlements, beautiful place in the mountains, city of pines and spruce, snow and ice, quartz, crystal, perhaps it survives somehow, protected by our people on the plane of air.
DM: Perhaps there might be a way to bring it back.
Seeker: How does, how does one travel to the plane of air?
Delwath: Do you know if there are other survivors?
DM: There are some. The thirty-seventh generation is not lost entirely.
Delwath: Do you know if, uh, do you know of Rathion? Do you know him? Or, or Drago?
DM: Am I supposed to know these names?
Delwath: I'm just making names up. They would be...
DM: They're Delwath's friend, like, friends of Delwath. Okay.

Delwath: They're just random people I'm ma- ma- making up right now. You can decide how, how, how, how dark is Delwath's current life. Are his fri-- Is everybody he was close to all dead? He could not know them.
DM: I do not know Rathion.
((table interruptions, repeated questions and unrelated planning))
DM: Last one, I, I know him. I fought with him in the wars. Pete-
((table interruptions, repeated questions and unrelated planning))
DM: ... would be thematically appropriate for him to opt dead.

He returned. He was, he was one of those in our generation who turned inward after the wars. There are some hidden cities left, a few, mostly north of here, Forest of Dreams. Small, nothing like the grand cities of old. Hidden.
Delwath: Do you know how to find them?

DM: I'm sure they would not be hidden to you. I, I could not face a lifetime of turning inward after my children were born and left their body parents to join their generation mates. Left their what? Body parents? Their body parents.
DM: I left again. They are hidden in a small camp in the north, I, I suspect. I haven't spoken to them in quite some time. I, I needed to know what was left of the world.
Delwath: To me, the war was only years ago, a small number, one, two. I was in the Shadowfell since the Great War until nine months ago when I met these folks.
DM: How did that thing happen?

Delwath: I suspect, uh... I was, um, I was the quartermaster of a company of elves. We encountered a hobgoblin party, and a great battle was fought. All of the elves died save me. All the hobgoblins died.
And as I was trying to pick through the bodies and uncover the body of my commander, she was lying underneath this great hobgoblin general. I touched something on his arm by accident.

Delwath: And it transported me to the Shadowfell, where I was trapped re- reliving the battle for what felt like several lifetimes until a god, Yezali as he was known, or as they were known, but now taking the name Aaviskar, somehow also trapped there.
I think, I think he was one of the... That he, they were one of the Tanshi. I'm sure they were one of the Tanshi, and somehow they found a way to send me out.
DM: She has mentioned that name.
Delwath: I would very much like to meet her.
Delwath: In visions, I saw him, I saw them die defending their people, but also touched the bane of a great, by a great demon, and appeared in the Shadowfell.
DM: A great demon? I fought many demons after the war. I fear there was some portal to the abyss in Pandar, fueled Cha'mutte's reign, perhaps fueled his control over the kenku.
Delwath: Dan, do you still think we can pull it through this?
Wellby: Uh, it makes it seem like a worse and worse mistake.
Wellby: Give a scroll of Connect Abyss to this plane.
Wellby: I guess that's kind of what I meant. That's fair. That's fair.
DM: I mean, it's not better.
Delwath: It's, it's... I still think that if Fausto was working for Apollyon, Apollyon doesn't want to destroy Taelgar by crashing it.
DM: Yeah, remember Cha'mutte and Apollyon were enemies.
Delwath: Um, this demon I think was... He w- the demon was fighting with Cha'mutte before, I believe, Cha'mutte was defeated.
DM: But to the north, you think?
Delwath: North of here, near our home, I believe. So I just saw a vision that Yezali sent me.
DM: Perhaps the first to fall early in the war when the demons issued forth.
Delwath: I suspect as much. Have you met other elves who have come out in the world?
DM: There are not many of us. There is one false elf.
Delwath: The green dragon? You met him, I gather.
DM: I stayed with his tribe for a few weeks. He tried to enchant me. He tried to, he tried to put a geas, geas on me.
DM: A charm, a, a command to perform a task for him.

DM: It was come to this village and bring Jordo out to justice for refusing, for refusing to, for refusing to accept his rule. And of course, his magic failed. I believe he knew that elves were difficult to sway in such a way, but he tried anyway. You know, that moment I ran...
Delwath: ... did you, he changed to a dragon, right?
DM: Fortunately, I had fought dragons in the war. I was not wholly unprepared for such a thing. But he was far beyond my skill to face.
Delwath: Hmm. I never had the misfortune of fighting a dragon until yes, two, two days ago? Three days ago?
DM: Like three days ago, yeah.
Delwath: Three days ago. We, uh, did not expect him to change and were, I think, wholly unprepared.

DM: But I found this place, and I've been safe here now for five years now. S- no, more than that. I lose track of these human years. Almost 10 years. I was able to meet Jordo before he died. He was an old man when I came. He was, he was an impressive man.
Delwath: Do you know anything about where he got his jade?
DM: He found it in the forest embedded in a fallen god tree, they call them, one of the trees that were the homes of our people.
Delwath: Do you know what it is?
DM: No. It has something to do with dreams, I believe.
Delwath: My friend Kenzo has another piece of the, the same jade.
DM: Do you know what it is?
Kenzo: Uh, it's in my soul item.

DM: Um, he is, uh, although there's a tinge of sadness to everything he does, he is very happy to be speaking to another elf, and he is, his curiosity is piqued a little bit about this jade. He seems... I mean, elves are always somewhat tricky to read, but there's nothing... You know what? He seems pretty open and honest.
Wellby: He didn't, for example, get the geas, "Come here and kill Jordo."
DM: Well, Jordo died five years ago, so even if he was- Hmm. He could, um ... I mean, it lasts for, like, 30 days, right?
Delwath: Spend a feat and make sure he's not under any spells.
DM: He's not under any spells. He's not super strong. He's, like, level three or four. He's not, he's not as powerful as you, for sure.
Kenzo: Well, he's g- we're gonna need him in the battle against the, uh, dragon, so be good to have a sense of his abilities.
Delwath: I think the important thing is just that he's not currently under any compulsion.
Kenzo: Uh, what did he ask me again?
DM: What, what is the piece of jade? What is the jade?
Kenzo: What do you know of the Sorcerer Rai?
DM: I know he killed Cha'mutte with his companions.
DM: Fought in many wars to the south, not where we were fighting.
Kenzo: You've lived here for five years now. What's the relationship that the, uh... What's the name of this tribe again?
Kenzo: What's the relationship with the Te'kula and the Sorcerer Rai?

DM: Alayah speaks of him as a... [sighs] There's not a good word in your tongue to explain it. A, a, a friend, but a friend from a, from an older generation, a, a wiser friend, a, a, a friend who is... A, a friend who is an elder, who is a, um... There's no word. I, uh...
See, there's a word in Elvish that basically means, like, one of the originals, like, one of the very oldest elves from-
DM: ... from, like, the elves who've been around the- A, a friend who aspires to such heights.
Kenzo: Hmm. And what of the, uh, what's the name of the, um, the, the god they're, um, uh-
Kenzo: ... Aasimti. And, and what of Aasimti?
